rows.rule: knee → pelvis → trunk → shoulder IR → elbow → wrist, 10–60 ms apart

v7.v: knee -198, pelvis -156, trunk -106, shoulder ir -298, elbow -64, wrist -89 ms

flaws: Kinetic chain only half right. Legs → pelvis → trunk peak in order (42 and 50 ms apart). The arm end is wrong: shoulder internal rotation peaks 298 ms before contact, and the wrist peaks before the elbow. The arm keys are still v6's. The whole v6 swing is about 3× slower than a real serve (sweet spot 12 m/s, real 30–40 m/s), and speeding it up breaks the smoothness gate. That needs a new arm timing pass.

Trunk arch 22°, target 40–50°. It is measured as the knee–hip–neck bow at the racket's low point. Trunk lean is capped at −30° by the body's joint ranges, and the 40–50° target is an analogue from another sport, not a tennis measurement.

The ballistic gate passes by construction. The flight is an exact parabola, and the pelvis is solved so that the whole-body CoM sits on it. The gate proves the solver does this; it does not show the jump height is right. Rise 8.3 cm and flight 0.29 s are inside the measured ranges.
Knee bend at load. The right (back) knee reaches 67°, but the left (front) knee only reaches 59°, below the 65–80° range.
Contact height is 1.407 × body height, just inside 1.40–1.45. The arm is fully extended, so a higher contact needs a higher jump.
Loop resets. v7 ends 0.85 m inside the court, so the player jumps back to the start when the loop restarts.
Not gated yet: balance (support polygon) and whole-body angular momentum. The toss is the v6 toss, so the "20–30 cm further left and back than a flat serve" target is not checked.
Same solver on both sides. v6 runs on the v7 solver unchanged, and its v6 gate numbers match the published v6 exactly (smoothness 334).
